thread:
Maya: Quick question — we're seeing inconsistent slice assignments when an A/B is scoped to tier=gold + region=eu-west. Some requests get routed to fallback variant even though capacity shows available. Anyone seen this?

Sam: Seen that before. Suspect ordering of checks: quota vs sampling. Can you paste the rollout config?

Maya: Here: ```json\n{\n  \"policy\": \"tier_region_routing\",\n  \"scope\": {\"tier\": \"gold\", \"region\": \"eu-west\"},\n  \"variant\": \"candidate-v2\",\n  \"fallback\": \"stable-v1\",\n  \"exposure\": 0.10\n}\n```\n
Olivia: The UI shows exposure 10% (global). Is that per-scope or global? If it's global and sampling happens before scoping, you'll see mismatches.

Lee: Reminder of our runtime flow: entitlement -> routing policy -> compute_shard -> quota_check -> assign_instance -> capacity_check -> fallback. If quota_check happens after compute_shard we can evict to fallback late.

Ana: Another angle — canary sampler seed currently uses hash(account_id + variant_key). But console rollout uses hash(account_id + tier + region). Seeds mismatch -> different membership sets.

Maya: That would explain why some gold-eu users appear in console AB but runtime puts them to fallback.

Sam: Proposed fixes: 1) canonicalize seed inputs across Console, Router, and Canary sampler to [account_id, tier, region, rollout_id] 2) move quota_check earlier if cheap 3) add telemetry for 'seed_inputs' in trace.

Olivia: UX follow-up: Console needs per-tier+region exposure breakdown (a table). Right now it shows global exposure only which is misleading for scoped rollouts.

Lee: Also consider fallback ordering: prefer same-region fallback variant before global fallback to preserve data residency and latency. Current code falls back to any compatible variant which can be cross-region.

Maya: Good point. For many enterprise customers regional affinity matters. Should be: try same-tier same-region > same-tier other-region > lower-tier same-region > global.

Sam: We'll need API changes for rollout status to expose computed_weights: {"gold:eu-west":0.10, "gold:us-west":0.0, ...}. Make it opt-in to preserve backward compat.

Ana: Unit test idea: simulate 100k faux requests with seeded account_ids and verify membership percentiles per (tier,region) match console computed exposures within +/-0.5%.

Maya: Agreed. Also add a small canary experiment to run in staging for 24h and compare telemetry: decision.cause (sampling|quota|capacity) counts.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary-router-service v2.14 -> staging (hash: a1b2c3) at 2024-11-09T15:43:12Z :rocket:

Olivia: We should also instrument the router to emit fallback_reason tags (e.g., quota_exhausted, capacity_unavailable, seed_mismatch). That will make postmortems much easier.

Lee: Edge-case: what if quota is soft (best-effort) and capacity_check is strict? Order matters. Need consistent semantics: quota should be a pre-check for exposure, not a dynamic runtime eviction unless marked.

Sam: I found a small off-by-one bug in the jitter window that can push ~0.2% of users across boundary — will include in patch.

Maya: I'll open the PR with tests + telemetry + console mockup screenshots. Also adding migration notes for rollout API consumers.

Olivia: Can someone add a small sim script? If not I'll hack one quick. We want distribution and fallback_reason breakdown.

Lee: I'll run the sim overnight and post numbers. Will also test regional-first fallback heuristic.

Ana: I'll review the PR tonight. If we agree on canonical seed format I'll update the canary sampler module.

Maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4287 (draft) — contains seed canonicalization, unit tests, and console wireframes.

Sam: Added unit tests in the PR; found another jitter edge. Pushed a small fix.

Maya: Thanks. Plan: land after CI + staging sim. Aim for canary-week next Mon. :thumbsup:

Olivia: One last ask — add a tiny endpoint that returns "computed_exposures" for a given rollout id so SRE can query current effective exposure per-scope programmatically.

Maya: Will add as opt-in field in rollout GET.

Lee: follow-up item: tag routing traces with sla_level for quick incident filtering.

Maya: OK, created tasks in the routing board and added owners. Will keep thread updated.
